name: FaceIQ Labs

card.summary: A face-rating YouTube channel and paid analysis brand that gives viewers measured feedback and looksmaxxing suggestions on facial features, weight, skin and procedures.
card.note: Ratings are subjective opinions; paid rating and advice products are sold through the brand.

quick.overview:
FaceIQ Labs is a looksmaxxing YouTube channel and brand known for rating subscribers' faces and proposing improvements. It is described as offering analysis based on dozens of facial measurements and sells paid ratings and a community space.

For people trying to improve their looks, it functions as outside feedback: videos suggest changes such as weight loss, skincare, dermatology or surgical options and point to where a face differs from commonly cited ideals. Within forums the channel draws both devoted followers and critics.
quick.how: Viewers watch rating videos, submit photos for review, or buy a paid rating and advice plan sold through Gumroad. Followers typically use the feedback to decide which self-improvement steps to prioritise.
quick.risks: Face ratings are opinions rather than medical assessments, and forum users disagree about their accuracy. Some forum members also criticise the host's tone. Advice involving procedures should be discussed with qualified clinicians.

lead: FaceIQ Labs, often shortened to FaceIQ, is a face-rating channel and brand in the looksmaxxing community. Its videos rate viewers' faces and suggest improvements, and a summary of one video describes recommendations ranging from weight loss and dermatology to rhinoplasty and eyebrow transplants [1]. A second summary describes a video rating three men with suggestions such as fat grafting and otoplasty [1].

The brand is also described as a paid platform with 100+ facial metrics across four structural pillars and a community space called the Loop, with Gumroad listings for a rating plus advice priced at $50 and a separate rating at $10 [1].

On looksmax.org, threads debate the channel's accuracy and style, with titles such as 'how accurate is faceiq labs', 'is faceiq the best rater ever' and 'what are your thoughts on faceiq' [3][4][5]. One thread asks why people watch face-analysis videos in their free time, and a reply says the uploader's daily videos make them happy [2].

chain: Face is rated against commonly cited metrics
Viewer learns which features and routines to target
Chooses skincare, weight, hair or procedure changes
angle.text: FaceIQ provides outside ratings and improvement suggestions, which viewers use to decide where to focus their self-improvement efforts.

infobox: Rating plans via Gumroad ($10 and $50 listings) [1]

paras: Videos present face ratings with commentary on structure, soft tissue and grooming, and propose interventions [1].

Forum threads include praise, with one poster saying they enjoy his daily uploads [2], and criticism of his approach, with titles questioning his accuracy or his own physique [3]. A reviewer of AI face raters wrote that FaceIQ's tool dominates the YouTube looksmaxxing ecosystem and said creators earn referrals; that claim is that blogger's opinion [1].

lore.intro: FaceIQ is a recurring topic on looksmax.org in threads about face rating and rater credibility [3][4].

claims.claim: FaceIQ is one of the best raters
claims.believers: Fans say they enjoy the content and consider the ratings useful [2][4].
claims.experts: No published studies have evaluated the accuracy of this channel's ratings.
